featureName: Household Profiles and Scoped Immich Credentials
summary: Permit each family member to use PhotoDesk through an authenticated household profile backed by that person's own user-scoped Immich API key. Review sessions, reviewed state, edits, and caches remain private to the profile even when Immich partner sharing makes household photos visible in a combined timeline.

fieldLearning.finding: Immich metadata search includes assets from timeline-enabled partners. Visibility does not imply mutation access: the connected user's key could preview partner assets but could not trash, rate, or stack them.
fieldLearning.mvpMitigation: Single-user PhotoDesk discovery now filters search results to AssetResponseDto.ownerId matching GET /api/users/me. New sessions persist ownerId, old unscoped discovery caches are invalidated, and legacy mixed-owner sessions are rejected before commit performs any Immich mutation.
fieldLearning.futureImplication: Partner timeline support must remain an explicit, ownership-labeled, capability-aware scope. It cannot reuse the owned-library commit model.

productIntent: The household can share photos through Immich without forcing everyone to operate as the Immich administrator.
Each person gets an independent PhotoDesk workspace and can review the same shared photo independently.
Immich remains the authority for asset visibility and mutation permissions; PhotoDesk does not invent broader access.
Parents can provision, disable, and recover household profiles without gaining routine access to another person's plaintext API key.

identityProvider.decision: Port the familyPulse passphrase/session pattern to SQLite
identityProvider.details: scrypt hash via node:crypto (salt:hash format), UUID session token, HttpOnly cookie named pd_session, 30-day TTL. Middleware resolves req.profile from cookie on every request. No external auth deps.
identityProvider.reference: familyPulse/lib/auth.js — hashPassphrase, verifyPassphrase, createSession, validateSession, requireAuth, requireParent

credentialStorage.decision: Store Immich API key plaintext in the profiles table, guarded by a secrets-guard module
credentialStorage.details: Same approach as familyPulse stores Plaid access tokens. The key is written once during enrollment, never returned in API responses, and redacted from logs by a secrets-guard module (pattern: familyPulse/lib/secrets-guard.js). The DB file lives on the LAN server alongside the .env that would hold any encryption key, so encryption at rest adds marginal value for this deployment. If a future deployment needs at-rest encryption, add it as a follow-up without changing the API surface.

defaultLibraryScope.decision: Default to the active user's owned library
defaultLibraryScope.details: Partner timeline inclusion is deferred to slice 3. Owned-only scope is already enforced by PR #4 and carries forward per-profile.

childAdministration.decision: Parents can create, disable, and reset profile passphrases. Kids manage their own Immich key enrollment after parent creates the profile.
childAdministration.details: Parents see all profiles in settings but cannot view another profile's sessions, decisions, or Immich key. Disabling a profile expires its session immediately. Passphrase reset by parent sets a temporary passphrase the kid changes on next login.

rejectedDirections.option: One Immich administrator API key with a user picker in PhotoDesk
rejectedDirections.reason: The picker would be cosmetic authorization. Every request and write would still execute with administrator authority, making profile isolation fragile and audit trails misleading.

rejectedDirections.option: Store API keys in localStorage or send them with browser requests
rejectedDirections.reason: This exposes durable Immich credentials to browser storage, XSS, extensions, screenshots, and client logs.

rejectedDirections.option: Encrypt API keys at rest with a master key
rejectedDirections.reason: Over-engineered for a LAN family app. The DB file sits on the same server as the .env that would hold the encryption key. The secrets-guard pattern (never return keys in API responses, redact from logs) provides the meaningful protection layer.

rejectedDirections.option: Use Immich account passwords as PhotoDesk credentials
rejectedDirections.reason: PhotoDesk should not collect or retain Immich passwords. User-created API keys provide revocation and granular permission controls.
The stated use case requires each person to have their own sessions. Household-shared review state could be a later explicit collaboration mode, not the default.

currentSingleUserAssumptions.impact: One process-wide IMMICH_API_KEY and IMMICH_URL are used for every request.
currentSingleUserAssumptions.resolution: Config retains IMMICH_URL (server-wide). IMMICH_API_KEY becomes the bootstrap key for the migration profile only; after migration, per-profile keys are read from the DB.

currentSingleUserAssumptions.impact: Authentication headers are built from the global configuration rather than request/profile context.
currentSingleUserAssumptions.resolution: Immich client functions accept an apiKey parameter or a profile context object. The global config fallback is removed after migration.

currentSingleUserAssumptions.impact: Sessions have no owner/profile foreign key.
currentSingleUserAssumptions.resolution: Add profile_id NOT NULL to sessions table. Migration backfills existing sessions to the bootstrap admin profile.

currentSingleUserAssumptions.impact: processed_assets uses asset_id as a global primary key, so one person's commit currently marks the asset reviewed for everyone.
currentSingleUserAssumptions.resolution: Rebuild table with UNIQUE(profile_id, asset_id) replacing the asset_id PRIMARY KEY. See migrationPlan.

currentSingleUserAssumptions.impact: There is one cached library snapshot and one global processed-asset set.
currentSingleUserAssumptions.resolution: Change density_cache PK from CHECK(id=1) singleton to UNIQUE(profile_id). Each profile gets its own snapshot with its own Immich key's view.

columns: role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(role IN ('parent', 'kid')) DEFAULT 'kid'
immich_url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' -- inherits server-wide IMMICH_URL if empty
immich_api_key TEXT -- plaintext, never returned in API responses
immich_user_id TEXT -- cached from GET /api/users/me after enrollment
immich_verified_at TEXT -- last successful credential check
status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('active', 'disabled', 'setup')) DEFAULT 'setup'
profiles.notes: A profile in 'setup' status has been created by a parent but has no Immich key enrolled yet. The kid logs in and enrolls their own key.

columns: profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
auth_sessions.notes: Named auth_sessions to avoid collision with the existing review sessions table. Cookie: pd_session, HttpOnly, 30-day TTL.

ownershipChanges: sessions: ADD COLUMN profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES profiles(id) DEFAULT 1 — backfill all existing rows to bootstrap admin profile (id=1)

processed_assets: rebuild table — new schema is (asset_id TEXT NOT NULL, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES profiles(id), session_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id), committed_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')), UNIQUE(profile_id, asset_id)). Copy existing rows with profile_id=1.
density_cache: change from CHECK(id=1) singleton to profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES profiles(id). Existing row gets profile_id=1.
Decisions, ratings, stacks, edits, commit_actions, commit_runs derive profile through their session's profile_id — no direct profile_id column needed.

migrationPlan.name: 005-household-profiles.sql
migrationPlan.strategy: Single transactional migration that creates new tables and adapts existing ones
steps: CREATE TABLE profiles with columns above
INSERT bootstrap admin profile (id=1) using display_name from env or 'Admin', role='parent', status='active', immich_api_key from current config, immich_url from current config
ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 REFERENCES profiles(id)

Rebuild processed_assets: CREATE processed_assets_new → INSERT INTO ... SELECT asset_id, 1 as profile_id, session_id, committed_at FROM processed_assets → DROP processed_assets → ALTER TABLE processed_assets_new RENAME TO processed_assets → recreate indexes

Rebuild density_cache: CREATE density_cache_new(profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES profiles(id), computed_at TEXT NOT NULL, data TEXT NOT NULL) → migrate existing row with profile_id=1 → drop and rename
CREATE secrets-guard index: CREATE INDEX idx_auth_sessions_token ON auth_sessions(token)
migrationPlan.rollbackNotes: SQLite does not support transactional DDL for all operations. The migration runner should back up the DB file before applying. If interrupted, restore from backup.

secretsGuard.pattern: Port from familyPulse/lib/secrets-guard.js, adapted for PhotoDesk
secretsGuard.usage: Call assertNoSecrets(rows) before sending any DB query results to API responses. Wrap error messages with sanitizeString() before logging.

immichClientChanges.approach: Add a profileContext parameter to all Immich client functions
details: Each exported function gains an optional first parameter: { apiKey, immichUrl }
If omitted, falls back to config (preserves backward compat during migration, removed after)
authHeaders() becomes authHeaders(apiKey) — no longer reads global config
The Express middleware resolves the profile, attaches req.profile with the decrypted key, and downstream route handlers pass it to Immich client calls

loginScreen.route: GET / when no valid pd_session cookie
loginScreen.design: Centered card on --bg-deep background. PhotoDesk wordmark + icon at top. List of active profile names as clickable buttons (like a user picker). Clicking a name shows a passphrase input field and a Login button. No profile creation from the login screen — parents do that in settings.
loginScreen.styling: Reuse existing design tokens, .btn, .btn-primary, .btn-ghost classes. Hanken Grotesk font. Passphrase input uses the same input styling as the session name input.
loginScreen.mobile: The card should be full-width on small viewports with comfortable touch targets.

profileIndicator.location: Header bar, next to the existing Immich connection pill
profileIndicator.design: Display name + avatar emoji in a pill. Clicking opens a small dropdown with 'Switch profile' and 'Log out'. Same styling as connection-pill.
profileIndicator.behavior: Switch profile logs out the current session and returns to the login screen.

adminSettings.location: New section in a Settings screen (gear icon in header, visible to parent role only)
capabilities: List all profiles with status, Immich connection health, and last active time
Create new profile (display name, role, temporary passphrase)
adminSettings.notIncluded: No ability to view another profile's sessions, decisions, or Immich key

credentialEnrollment.location: Shown automatically when a 'setup' status profile logs in, or accessible from a personal settings area
credentialEnrollment.flow: Paste Immich API key → PhotoDesk calls GET /api/users/me with it to verify → shows Immich username for confirmation → saves key and immich_user_id on confirm
credentialEnrollment.guidance: Include a short help text explaining where to find the API key in Immich (Administration → API Keys)

deliverySlices.name: Compatibility and threat-model spike
deliverySlices.outcome: Document the deployed Immich version, required API-key permission set, current-user/key verification calls, partner timeline retrieval, asset ownership fields, and mutation behavior for partner-owned assets.
deliverySlices.notes: PR #4 already validated ownership filtering, getCurrentUser(), and the mutation boundary. Remaining work: document the minimum Immich API key permission set PhotoDesk requires, and verify getMyApiKey endpoint returns granted permissions.
exitCriteria: Every PhotoDesk Immich endpoint is mapped to its required API-key permission
Minimum permission template documented for user-facing key creation guidance
Owned versus partner-owned write behavior tested (done in PR #4)

deliverySlices.name: Profiles, auth, credential enrollment, and migration
deliverySlices.outcome: Add profile login/session management, secrets-guard module, per-profile Immich credential enrollment, admin profile management, and the single-user migration.
deliverySlices.scopeLimit: Owned Immich library only. Existing single-user PhotoDesk workflows remain unchanged after migration. The only new UI is the login screen, profile indicator, admin settings, and credential enrollment.
exitCriteria: Migration 005 creates profiles/auth_sessions tables, backfills existing data to a bootstrap admin profile, and rebuilds processed_assets and density_cache with profile_id
Migration is tested fresh, on existing single-user DB, and idempotent rerun
Login screen lists active profiles, accepts passphrase, sets pd_session cookie
All existing API routes require auth and resolve req.profile from session
Immich client functions accept per-profile credentials instead of global config
Credential enrollment verifies key against Immich and persists immich_user_id
secrets-guard module redacts API keys and passphrases from responses and logs
Parent can create/disable profiles and reset passphrases from admin settings
Disabling a profile immediately expires its auth session
Automated tests cover: two-profile isolation, login/logout, credential enrollment, disabled profile rejection, secrets-guard redaction
Browser tests cover: login flow, profile switching, admin CRUD, credential enrollment, mobile login

deliverySlices.name: Per-profile PhotoDesk state isolation
deliverySlices.outcome: Partition sessions, reviewed assets, discovery snapshots, recent sessions, edits, and commits by profile.
exitCriteria: Creating a session records the active profile_id
Library discovery and density cache are keyed by profile_id
processed_assets uses UNIQUE(profile_id, asset_id) — one profile's commit does not mark assets reviewed for other profiles
Session list, recent sessions, and all session-scoped API routes are filtered to the active profile
Automated tests prove: Profile A commits an asset, Profile B still sees it as unreviewed. Profile A's sessions are invisible to Profile B's API requests.
Browser test: two profiles each see independent library stats and session lists

deliverySlices.name: Partner timeline discovery
deliverySlices.outcome: Offer an explicit per-profile owned/partner timeline scope, show ownership badges, and keep unsupported mutations disabled.
deliverySlices.scopeLimit: Read/discovery first; commit support is capability-gated.
exitCriteria: Profile settings include a library scope toggle (owned-only vs owned+partners)
Partner assets are visually distinguished in grid, lightbox, and summary with an ownership badge
Commit preview disables and explains unsupported actions for partner-owned assets
Discovery cache is keyed by profile_id + library_scope
Automated tests cover: partner asset visibility with badge, commit rejection for partner assets, scope toggle cache invalidation

deliverySlices.name: Capability-aware shared workflows
deliverySlices.outcome: Enable only the partner/shared-asset operations proven safe and supported by Immich, with clear commit previews and audit records.
deliverySlices.scopeLimit: Do not broaden permissions through an administrator credential.
exitCriteria: Each commit action type (trash, rate, stack, edit upload) is individually gated by asset ownership and API key permissions
Commit preview shows per-asset capability breakdown with clear explanations for disabled actions
Automated tests cover: mixed owned/partner session with selective commit
Browser test: commit preview accurately reflects which actions are allowed per asset

acceptanceCriteria: Profile A cannot list, retrieve, mutate, or infer Profile B's PhotoDesk sessions, decisions, ratings, edits, caches, or credentials.
The same Immich asset can be reviewed independently by two profiles and remains unreviewed for Profile B after Profile A commits it.
No normal browser request can choose another profile's Immich credential through a path, query, header, or request body value.
API keys are never returned after enrollment and are redacted from logs and error messages.
PhotoDesk verifies and records the Immich user identity associated with each submitted key.
A disabled profile immediately loses PhotoDesk access without disrupting other household members.
Discovery and density caches are isolated by profile and selected library scope.
Shared partner assets are visibly distinguished from owned assets before review and commit.
Unsupported writes to partner-owned assets are prevented and explained before commit.
The existing single-user database migrates to one household administrator profile without losing sessions, reviewed state, edits, or commit history.
Automated tests cover two profiles with overlapping visible asset IDs and prove state isolation.
Browser tests cover profile switching, session isolation, credential enrollment, and mobile login.
libraryAndCommitRules: The active profile's Immich key determines the assets visible to PhotoDesk.
Owned-library discovery and review should ship before partner-aware writes.
If partner assets are enabled, label asset ownership in discovery, workspace, editor, and commit summary.
Compute commit actions per asset from both API-key permissions and asset ownership/capability evidence.
Disable unsupported actions before commit and explain why; do not rely on an Immich 403 after the user finishes a session.

Rendered derivatives upload into the active Immich user's account. Do not stack a derivative with a partner-owned original until that behavior is verified against the deployed Immich version and product semantics are approved.
Cache keys and background refresh jobs must include profile_id and library_scope.

researchReferences.title: FamilyPulse auth pattern
